lang.name: English
meta.description: Proks is a caching HTTP proxy in Go: TinyLFU eviction, Markov-chain prefetching, invalidation via RabbitMQ.
theme.label: Color theme
home.lead: A caching HTTP proxy in Go. It serves cache hits in a few microseconds, predicts which page will be requested next, and purges stale data on every replica at once.
home.about_p1: Proks sits between clients and your API. Repeated GET requests are served from memory without touching the upstream. Responses with Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie or Cache-Control: private bypass the cache, so one user's private data never reaches another.
home.about_p2: The proxy knows nothing about your domain: purge tags come from the route config or from upstream headers (Surrogate-Key, Cache-Tag). That makes it fit any HTTP API.
home.stat_p95: HTTP p95 on a local setup
home.stat_note: Measured on Intel Core i7-10870H with Go benchmarks and k6.
home.f1_p: The proxy learns transitions between pages and, after a request for A, fetches the likely next route B in advance while the user is still reading A.
home.f1_foot: p95 of the second request in a chain −22%
home.f2_p: The cache keeps keys that are requested often, not just recently. A one-off scan over thousands of pages does not push hot entries out of memory.
home.f2_foot: hit ratio 0.457 vs 0.260 for LRU under a scan load
home.f3_p: A change in the database goes to a transactional outbox and is broadcast to every replica. Events survive a broker outage, and duplicates are dropped by event_id.
docs.note: The documentation is written in Russian and is shown as it is in the repository.
bench.lead: A/B test of Markov-chain prefetching: the “book card → its authors” scenario (k6/prefetch-chain.js) with prefetching off and on.
bench.about: The benchmark runs in GitHub Actions weekly and on every release: a Docker setup with PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ, 20 s warm-up, 1 minute per mode. GitHub runners are shared and noisy, so watch the trend rather than a single point. The key metric is p95 of the second request in the chain (authors).
